A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: Same-day chest X-ray report with immediate CT. A radiologist or reporting radiographer reads primary-care chest X-rays while the patient waits; if suspicious, CT is done the same day or within days and the referral is triggered by radiology.
effect_summary_en: In a randomised trial in London, published in Thorax in 2023, the median time from chest X-ray to lung cancer diagnosis was 32 days with immediate reporting and 63 days with standard reporting, a saving of 31 days (p=0.03, 49 cancers).
supported_en: A randomised trial in Thorax (2023) found a 31-day shorter median time from chest X-ray to diagnosis (32 vs 63 days).
not_supported_en: There is no confidence interval, and the trial is from one London hospital, not a Finnish or rural setting.
in_use_summary_en: No public sign was found that same-day chest X-ray reporting with direct CT runs in Lapha or at OYS; Lapha's CT page describes an ordinary booked CT whose results come from the referring unit.
summary_en: No public sign was found that Lapha or OYS already reads chest X-rays the same day and sends suspicious cases straight to CT; Lapha's lung CT page describes a booked scan whose results come from the referring unit. A randomised trial in Thorax (2023) found that reporting the X-ray at once halved the median time from chest X-ray to lung cancer diagnosis, from 63 to 32 days.
unanswered_en: Two OYS lung pages could not be opened (HTTP 404), so the OYS pathway for chest X-ray findings was not checked.
